setup.zh: 开春，舅舅从县城来，念了一张告示：沉鼎观开山门，录为弟子者，家里每年五两银子。他刚念到「沉鼎」，你胸口的木牌烫得像一块炭。
setup.en: In spring Uncle comes from the county town and reads out a notice: Chending Temple opens its gate, and a disciple's family gets five taels a year. At the words "Chending" the token at your chest burns like a coal.

recap.zh: 舅舅带来了沉鼎观开山门的告示；他念到「沉鼎」，木牌烫得像炭——你决定去。
recap.en: Uncle brought the notice that Chending Temple would open its gate; at "Chending" the token burned like a coal — and you decided to go.

zh: 舅舅：簇新的青布长衫，二斤肉，一包红糖。
en: Uncle: a brand-new blue gown, two jin of meat, a packet of brown sugar.
"…present themselves for trial at the foot of Chending Mountain."
Between your fingers, a thread of silver light.

story.zh:
开春的时候，舅舅来了。

舅舅是你娘的亲弟弟，在县城济世堂做账房，是你们家这一门亲戚里，唯一一个「出息了」的人。他穿一身簇新的青布长衫，手里提着二斤肉、一包红糖，站在你家门口，看了看那扇装歪了的门，拿袖子掩着鼻子，咳了一声。

你爹慌慌张张地拿袖子擦炕沿，擦了三遍，请他坐。

舅舅坐下了。屁股只沾了半边。另外半边，悬在空中，随时准备撤退。

他看了看屋顶，看了看墙角接水的那一排盆，又看了看你爹缠着麻布的膝盖，长长地叹了一口气。

**舅舅**：姐，你这日子……

**娘**：挺好。

**舅舅**：屋顶都漏成这样了——

**娘**：通风。

**舅舅**：……

吃饭的时候，舅舅从怀里摸出一张折得方方正正的纸。

**舅舅**：县城贴的告示。我给你们抄了一份。

他清了清嗓子，念：

「**沉鼎观**，三年一开山门，收徒。凡十二至十六岁、身家清白者，皆可于九月初九，赴泗水沉鼎山下应试。录为弟子者，其家每岁由观中发给白银五两——」

他刚念到「沉鼎」两个字——

你胸口的木牌，烫得像一块刚从灶膛里扒出来的炭。

「嗷——！」

你从凳子上蹦了起来，一口饭喷了舅舅一脸。

屋里，安静了。

舅舅坐在那儿，脸上挂着饭粒，一动不动。一粒米从他的眉毛上，慢慢地滑了下来。

**你**：（捂着胸口）……噎、噎着了。

**舅舅**：（很慢很慢地擦脸）这孩子。吃个饭都吃不利索。

没有人看见，你捂在胸口的手指缝里，漏出了一线银光。

木牌上那条银色的尾巴，不再一明一暗了。它亮着，一直亮着，亮得发烫——像一个在梦里找了很久很久的人，终于听见了自己要找的那个名字。

---

**娘**：五两银子？

**舅舅**：一年五两。

你爹放下了筷子。你家一年交马家的租，折成银子，二两多一点。

**舅舅**：（压低声音）还有。家里有孩子进了仙门的——马家，不敢收租。

屋里静了。

**舅舅**：姐。二十年前，我也去过。

你们全愣住了。

**舅舅**：三百级石阶。我爬到一百六十级，腿就动不了了。我在那儿坐了一炷香，看着别人一个一个从我身边走过去。然后我就下山了，去济世堂学打算盘。

**娘**：（轻轻地）上回你说是一百五十级。

**舅舅**：……一百六十级。

**娘**：上上回，一百四十。

**舅舅**：（脸红了）每年都在长嘛！人老了，记性好了！

**爹**：（真诚地）那再过几年，您就爬上去了。

舅舅瞪了你爹一眼。你爹低头吃饭。

舅舅转过头，看着你。

**舅舅**：你娘识字，你随她，脑子比我活。你爹打猎，你随他，腿脚比我稳。去试试。进不去，也不亏什么。进去了——

他没说完。他看了一眼你爹的膝盖，看了一眼墙角那一排盆，又低下头，吃饭了。
story.en:
When spring comes, Uncle comes.

Uncle is your mother's own younger brother, the bookkeeper at Jishi Hall in the county town — the only one in your family's whole tree of relatives who has "made something of himself." He stands at your door in a brand-new blue cotton gown, two jin of meat and a packet of brown sugar in hand, looks at the door you rehung crooked, holds his sleeve to his nose, and coughs.

Your father flusters about wiping the edge of the brick bed with his sleeve — three times — and asks him to sit.

Uncle sits. With half his backside. The other half hovers in the air, ready to retreat at any moment.

He looks at the roof, at the row of basins in the corner catching the leaks, at the hemp wound round your father's knee, and heaves a long sigh.

**Uncle:** Sister, the way you live…

**Mother:** It's fine.

**Uncle:** The roof leaks like a sieve —

**Mother:** Ventilation.

**Uncle:** …

At dinner, Uncle takes a neatly folded paper out of his gown.

**Uncle:** A notice they put up in town. I copied it out for you.

He clears his throat and reads:

"**Chending Temple** opens its gate once in three years to take disciples. All between twelve and sixteen years of age, of clean family, may present themselves for trial at the foot of Chending Mountain on the Si, on the ninth day of the ninth month. The family of any taken as a disciple shall receive from the temple five taels of silver each year —"

The instant he reaches the word "Chending" —

the token on your chest burns like a coal just raked out of the stove.

"Aaagh —!"

You shoot up off the stool and spray a mouthful of rice all over Uncle's face.

The room goes quiet.

Uncle sits there, rice stuck to his face, not moving. A single grain slides, very slowly, down off his eyebrow.

**You:** (clutching your chest) …W-went down the wrong way.

**Uncle:** (wiping his face very, very slowly) This child. Can't even eat a meal properly.

Nobody sees the thread of silver light leaking between the fingers pressed to your chest.

The silver tail on the token is no longer bright-then-dim. It's lit, and stays lit, burning hot — like someone who has searched a very long time in a dream and has finally heard the name they were looking for.

---

**Mother:** Five taels of silver?

**Uncle:** Five a year.

Your father puts down his chopsticks. Your family's yearly rent to the Mas, reckoned in silver, is a little over two taels.

**Uncle:** (lowering his voice) And. A family with a child in an immortals' sect — the Mas wouldn't dare collect rent from them.

The room goes quiet.

**Uncle:** Sister. Twenty years ago, I went too.

All of you stare at him.

**Uncle:** Three hundred steps. I got to the hundred-and-sixtieth and my legs wouldn't move. I sat there for a stick of incense, watching the others go past me one by one. Then I came down the mountain and went to Jishi Hall to learn the abacus.

**Mother:** (gently) Last time you said it was the hundred-and-fiftieth.

**Uncle:** …Hundred-and-sixtieth.

**Mother:** The time before that, a hundred and forty.

**Uncle:** (going red) It grows every year! You get older, your memory gets better!

**Father:** (sincerely) Then in a few more years, you'll be at the top.

Uncle glares at your father. Your father bends over his rice.

Uncle turns and looks at you.

**Uncle:** Your mother can read, and you take after her — your head's quicker than mine. Your father hunts, and you take after him — your legs are steadier than mine. Go and try. If you don't get in, you've lost nothing. If you do —

He doesn't finish. He glances at your father's knee, at the row of basins in the corner, and bends over his rice again.

exits.means: decides to go to the temple trials

story.zh:
那天夜里，你躺在炕上，一直睁着眼睛。

你在心里算账。像你娘教你的那样，一笔一笔地算。

五两银子，一年。你爹，再也不用拖着那条腿进深山。你娘，下雨天再也不用把家里所有的盆摆出来。马三的短棍，再也敲不到你家的门框。

然后，是另一笔账。

木牌上那条尾巴，还亮着。它从来没有亮得这么久过。

你把木牌从衣领里掏出来，贴在耳朵边上，听。

什么都听不见。

可你知道，它在等你。

**你**：（对着黑暗）好。我去。
story.en:
That night you lie on the brick bed with your eyes wide open.

You do the accounts in your head. The way your mother taught you: one entry at a time.

Five taels of silver, every year. Your father never again dragging that leg into the deep mountains. Your mother never again setting out every basin in the house when it rains. Ma San's club never again rapping on your door frame.

Then, the other account.

The tail on the token is still lit. It has never stayed lit this long.

You pull the token out from your collar and hold it to your ear. Listen.

Nothing.

But you know it's waiting for you.

**You:** (to the dark) All right. I'll go.

exits.means: hesitates, decides not to go yet, waits

story.zh:
**你**：（对着黑暗，小声）不去……家里离不开我。再等三年。

胸口的木牌，一下子凉了。

那条亮了一整晚的尾巴，暗了下去——一明，一暗，一明——暗下去的那一下，比平时长。

你睁着眼睛躺到天亮。隔着一道布帘，你爹咳了半夜。
story.en:
**You:** (quietly, to the dark) Not going… they can't manage without me here. Three more years.

The token on your chest goes cold at once.

The tail that has been lit all night dims — bright, dim, bright — and the dim lasts longer than it ever has.

You lie there with your eyes open until dawn. Behind the cloth curtain, your father coughs half the night.
